_: Non-blocking overrides. A finding listed here is still REPORTED but does not block a commit. Every waiver requires date, who and why — a waiver missing any of them is invalid and does not waive. `review_by` is optional; past it, the waiver still holds but is flagged, because a permanent waiver is how a check rots into decoration.

waivers.subject: divergence
waivers.why: One extraction run over one section is the only such run that exists. Recording it as n=1 is the honest state, not a defect to fix; it clears when a second run exists.

waivers.subject: flat_siblings
waivers.why: Same single extraction run as `divergence`. Clears with a second run.

waivers.subject: witness_scope
waivers.why: One rule in one hand-written translation. Clears when stage 1 has produced translations we did not write ourselves.

waivers.subject: reviewer_blind
waivers.why: One blind-reviewer trial. The finding it produced is structural rather than statistical — a clause-local reviewer cannot see an entity the clause never enumerates — so n=1 is weak evidence for a rate and adequate evidence for the mechanism. Do not quote it as a rate.

waivers.subject: completeness_ok
waivers.why: Same single trial as `reviewer_blind`. Clears alongside it.

waivers.subject: p13
waivers.why: A probe set is a test, not a proof: it cannot cover situations nobody wrote a case for. The residue is inherent to testing and is named in the model. Closing it would need whole-program equivalence checking (anthem-style), which is a real option and not this phase's work.

waivers.subject: p14
waivers.why: The rule-shape check catches a violated declaration; it cannot catch a claim nobody thought to declare. Detecting an undeclared claim is a reading of the clause, not a property of the program. Accepted as inherent; the completeness reviewer is the partial mitigation.

waivers.subject: p2
waivers.why: The link check catches 'referenced and absent'. It cannot catch 'should have been referenced and was not', because nothing mechanical knows what the translation ought to have used. The completeness reviewer is the mitigation and it is a judgement, not a floor.

waivers.subject: p1
waivers.why: No deterministic check can close invention. Requiring every symbol to resolve to a dictionary entry, and every entry to cite a real clause, narrows it — but an invention that mints an entry citing a real clause still resolves. Whether that clause ESTABLISHES the concept is a reading. Permanently seat-dependent.

waivers.subject: p13
waivers.why: Same residue as only_narrowed/p13. Over-permissiveness outside the probe set is not mechanically detectable without whole-program equivalence checking. Flagged as possibly closable later; not now.

waivers.subject: p14
waivers.why: Same residue as only_narrowed/p14. A claim nobody declared cannot be detected by checking declarations.

waivers.subject: p6
waivers.why: ⭐ No deterministic check is possible even in principle. Detecting that an encoding asserts the converse of a negative statement requires understanding what the clause says. This problem will always rest on a model judgement, and recording that is more useful than leaving it looking like an oversight.

waivers.subject: p9
waivers.why: Deciding whether two uses of one name MEAN the same thing is semantic. The divergence check narrows it by enumerating situations where two readings differ, but a uniformly-wrong reading has no twin to differ from. Concept identity (Invariant 1) is the structural mitigation, not a deterministic check.

waivers.subject: coverage_rule
waivers.why: Ruled on 2026-08-07 and correctly not built: its denominator is licence-dependent and facts do not carry licences yet. Tracked as blocked_by(invariant_2_unimplemented) in the model. This waiver should be REMOVED, not renewed, once licences land.
